content.text:
Hovering any figure at the top of the Divergence Report tab now shows a tooltip explaining it. The "92% aligned" in the header gets one too. Each tooltip shows the figure's name, then a short muted explanation wrapped to a readable width:

- **Aligned:** how closely the code and the spec agree: 100% minus the average divergence of every file analyzed. Green above 80%, amber above 50%, red otherwise.
- **Source definition:** how much of the code the spec defines, averaged over the source files. Low means the code filled in a lot the spec never says.
- **Spec definition:** how precisely the spec describes what to build, averaged over the spec files. Low means gaps the code has to guess at.
- **Source coverage:** the share of source files connected to at least one spec file. One with no connection isn't driven by the spec at all.
- **Spec coverage:** the share of spec files that at least one source file implements. One with no connection isn't built yet, or can't be traced to the code.
- **Aligned · Drifting · Diverged:** how many files are aligned (diverging under 20%), drifting (20% up to 50%), or diverged (50% or more).

The saved-reports test now hovers a figure, waits past the tooltip delay and checks the tooltip appears. It also checks every figure has an explanation. - **Aligned:** how closely the code and the spec agree: 100% minus the average divergence of every file analyzed. Green above 80%, amber above 50%, red otherwise.
- **Source definition:** how much of the code the spec defines, averaged over the source files. Low means the code filled in a lot the spec never says.
- **Spec definition:** how precisely the spec describes what to build, averaged over the spec files. Low means gaps the code has to guess at.
- **Source coverage:** the share of source files connected to at least one spec file. One with no connection isn't driven by the spec at all.
- **Spec coverage:** the share of spec files that at least one source file implements. One with no connection isn't built yet, or can't be traced to the code.
- **Aligned · Drifting · Diverged:** how many files are aligned (diverging under 20%), drifting (20% up to 50%), or diverged (50% or more).
